fix_commit_message:
avcodec/libdav1d: fix heap overflow in US ITU-T T.35 metadata parsing

The US country_code path in parse_itut_t35_metadata() reads the
the provider_code with bytestream2_get_be16u(), which is a
unchecked version that does not validate the remaining
length before reading. When an AV1 stream contains ITU-T T.35
metadata with country_code set to 0xB5 (which is US) and a
payload shorter than 2 bytes, this results in a heap overflow
reading 2 bytes past the allocation.

The UK country code already guards against this issue by
checking it before the unchecked read. We're using the same
pattern to the US country code path.

Pwno crafted an AV1 IVF with a metadata OBU containing ITU-T T.35
with country_code=0xB5 and a 1-byte payload. Decoding with libdav1d
triggers the overflow. ASan says:

ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
READ of size 2 at 0x5020000003f0 thread T0
  #0 bytestream_get_be16 src/libavcodec/bytestream.h:98
  #1 bytestream2_get_be16u src/libavcodec/bytestream.h:98
  #2 parse_itut_t35_metadata src/libavcodec/libdav1d.c:376

0x5020000003f1 is located 0 bytes after 1-byte region

Found-by: Pwno
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix e90c2ff4b5a5 on top of intro fe1ffd63fb09 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): parse_itut_t35_metadata() in libavcodec/libdav1d.c parses ITU-T T.35 metadata OBUs emitted by the dav1d AV1 decoder. For payloads whose country_code identifies the United States (ITU_T_T35_COUNTRY_CODE_US, 0xB5), the function reads a 16-bit provider_code from the payload buffer using bytestream2_get_be16u(), the unchecked variant of the bytestream2 API that performs no bounds checking against the remaining buffer length. If an attacker supplies a crafted AV1 bitstream containing an ITU-T T.35 metadata OBU with country_code = 0xB5 and a payload shorter than 2 bytes (e.g. 1 byte), the unchecked read walks past the end of the allocated payload buffer, triggering a heap-buffer-overflow read of up to 2 bytes as confirmed by AddressSanitizer. Root cause: During a refactor that converted the country_code/provider_code dispatch logic in parse_itut_t35_metadata() into nested switch statements, the previously bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() call used to read provider_code was replaced by the unchecked bytestream2_get_be16u() variant for the US country_code case, without adding an explicit length check (bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < 2) beforehand. The analogous branch for the UK country code does include such a guard, but it was inconsistently omitted for the US branch, leaving a gap where attacker-controlled short payloads are read out of bounds.
